channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Stevenage Braces for Life After GSK as Drugmaker Moves to Cambridge
item.description: Nursing a pint at a pub a short walk from GSK Plc’s research headquarters in Stevenage, 30 miles north of London, Paul Jamison is fretting about the British drugmaker’s campus becoming a wasteland. The town’s largest employer is leaving, with the majority of its 1,800 scientists and support staff moving to Cambridge.
item.dc:creator: Martin Alfonsin Larsen and Ashleigh Furlong

item.title: Musk Touts Starlink for India’s Rural Users Amid Stalled Launch
item.description: Billionaire Elon Musk pitched Starlink Inc.’s satellite-based internet service as a solution for India’s most underserved rural regions, even though the operator’s launch remains stalled in the country over security concerns.
item.dc:creator: Satviki Sanjay

item.title: Fujifilm Expands Key Chip Material Output to Capture AI Demand
item.description: Fujifilm Holdings Corp. is expanding production of key materials used in advanced semiconductor manufacturing to capitalize on surging demand.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Mochizuki

item.title: Can Anthropic Beat SpaceX’s Record IPO Size?
item.description: Anthropic expects to match or beat the size of SpaceX’s record-setting initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter, in the latest sign of overwhelming demand from investors looking to profit from the artificial intelligence boom. Anthony Stephens has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Phancy Group's Tseng Says AI Demand to Drive Growth
item.description: Maryann Tseng, Chief Strategy Officer at Phancy Group, says growing global demand for AI development will help drive the company's growth over the next several years. She speaks exclusively on "The China Show." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Spending Splurge Boosts Danfoss’s Bet on Data Center Cooling
item.description: Danfoss A/S expects its data-center business to at least double its share of the firm’s sales this year as the artificial-intelligence boom drives spending on the cooling equipment needed to run increasingly powerful chips.
item.dc:creator: Sara Sjolin

item.title: Can AI Solve Online Shopping’s Biggest Problem?
item.description:
When was the last time you ordered jeans online and they actually fit?
Brands hope that AI-powered tools will help deliver the perfect size, meaning happier customers and fewer returned goods. Sonja Wind explains how. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Johor Nets $1.2 Billion in Investment Bids After Singapore Visit
item.description: Malaysia’s Johor state has attracted more than 5 billion ringgit ($1.2 billion) in potential investments following meetings with investors during a recent working visit to Singapore, according to Onn Hafiz Ghazi, chief minister of the state.
item.dc:creator: Ram Anand

item.title: Samsung Set to Top Phone Market in Downturn, Counterpoint Says
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. will regain the top position in the smartphone market this year, in a sign of its greater resilience to higher memory-chip prices, Counterpoint Research predicted.
item.dc:creator: Vlad Savov

item.title: CXMT, AI Hardware Firms Take Helm as China Earnings Enter Peak
item.description: CXMT Corp.’s breakout listing has sparked optimism across the domestic artificial intelligence hardware space, supporting China’s strategic ambitions to challenge the US in AI development.
item.dc:creator: Felix Tam and Rachel Yeo

item.title: Alibaba Profit Dives 75% as AI Spending Ratchets Up
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s profit plunged more than 75% after the company increased quarterly capital spending to almost $10 billion to safeguard its position in the global AI arena. Bloomberg's Minmin Low reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Samsung Plans to Return Up to $79 Billion to Shareholders
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. plans to return as much as 110 trillion won ($79 billion) to shareholders, joining rival SK Hynix Inc. in handing investors a chunk of the windfall generated by the AI rush.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee and Youkyung Lee

item.title: Stocks Fall as Bond Yields Rise | The Close 8/20/2026
item.description: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Rockefeller Global Family Office CIO Jimmy Chang, Agility Robotics CEO Peggy Johnson, UBS Equity Research Analyst Michael Lasser, LVMH North America Former Chairman Pauline Brown, Laffer Tengler Investments CEO & CIO Nancy Tengler, Telsey Advisory Group CEO & Chief Research Officer Dana Telsey, J&J Snack Foods CEO Dan Fachner, & Open Machine CEO Allie Miller. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Maisonette Tackles "Untapped" Retail Market
item.description: The curated online marketplace Maisonette is expanding it to what it describes as an untapped market by launching a new platform targeted to tweens and teens. President AJ Nicholas saying the company is looking to tap into the demographic of kids that "start to exert some independence and autonomy and really have a say over their style." As Maisonette has been around for 9 years, Nicholas says its important that the company grows organically as its customers' families grow up as well, allowing them to expand further into the more than $225 Billion industry. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Open Machine CEO on Anthropic, OpenAI IPO Potential
item.description: Allie Miller, CEO of Open Machine, shared insights on how top technology companies are managing their AI investments to balance cost and return. She explained that frontier companies typically divide their AI efforts into two groups: one focused on raising the baseline capabilities across departments like finance, legal, marketing, and sales with modest subscription-level spending, and a second, smaller 'frontier' team that operates with significantly higher budgets and greater experimentation freedom. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bonds Fall on Doubts Over Treasury's Plan | Real Yield 8/20/2026
item.description: "Bloomberg Real Yield" highlights the market-moving news you need to know. Today's guests: Ian Lyngen, Head of US Rates Strategy at BMO Capital Markets, Stephanie Roth, Chief Economist at Wolfe Research, Meghan Robson, Head of US Credit Strategy at BNP Paribas, and Milwood Hobbs, Deputy CIO of Oaktree's Strategic Credit Platform. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Agility Robotics CEO on Plans To Go Public, China Rivals
item.description: Peggy Johnson, CEO of Agility Robotics, discussed the company's upcoming public debut, positioning it as the only pure-play US public company focused on humanoid robots with proven commercial applications. Agility Robotics is valued at a $2.5 billion pre-money valuation and expects to go public in the fall. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Sally Bakewell on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ChatGPT Can Now Control iMessage, Potentially Raising Apple Privacy Concerns
item.description: OpenAI rolled out support on Thursday for controlling Apple Inc.’s iMessage service via ChatGPT, a move with the potential to raise privacy concerns for the iPhone maker.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: OpenAI, Meta Seek Help to Combat Data Center PR Problem
item.description: Tech firms are trying to quell growing opposition to their AI plans
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: Apple’s AirPods Should Avoid Meta’s Mistakes
item.description: Bloomberg Opinion columnist Dave Lee explains Apple’s plans for AI-enhanced AirPods and smart glasses, and why the company should learn from Meta’s mistakes. (Source: Bloomberg)
